dod_intent_evidence: Two 2022 SBIR Phase IIs (Air Force NDE, Navy V-22 SIA QA) plus named USMC EOD, USCG, NSWC, and NAWCAD customers — SBIR record and homepage testimonials.
score_evidence: '300% reduction in errors, 90% reduction in time to train and 98% reduction in waste and rework' — demo-metric bragging with no fielding path → lab_language_intensity (homepage testimonial they chose to feature)
'Develop custom XR at lightning speed through our patented AI-powered XR no-code authoring platform' → lab_language_intensity (homepage)

'We will review the architecting of SIA QA to ensure its resilience against future needs (RMF and on-ramping to government systems)' — RMF acknowledged but deferred to a future review, not engineered in → partial deployment awareness (sbir_abstract)
No jobs data in pack → hiring_profile_skew set to exactly 10 per rule
'SBIR PhII x2 [2022]' with 29 employees and no follow-on production vehicle anywhere in the pack — both Phase II periods of performance have run out by 2026 → stage_pressure (channel notes)

blind_spots.blind_spot: Build-once-deploy-anywhere assumes commercial device deployment paths; Navy flightline and shipboard networks don't accept COTS AR headsets without per-device-type accreditation
blind_spots.operator_reality: A maintainer on a carrier deck or in a V-22 hangar can't pair a Wi-Fi-dependent headset to a SaaS backend; NMCI/RMF accreditation of the headset class and offline content delivery decide whether SIA QA ever leaves the demo room
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their own abstract defers RMF to a Phase II 'review' of architecture rather than designing for it; testimonials all come from lab/warfare-center engagements, not fleet squadrons
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Its build-once, deploy-anywhere capability streamlines the process and maximizes efficiency across platforms.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'SaaS and on-prem platforms' — the SaaS half assumes connectivity that afloat and expeditionary maintenance environments deny
blind_spots.operator_reality: The 'Should-Be' database that SIA QA compares against in real time has to live and update on a disconnected local node; a ship underway gets intermittent SATCOM at best — same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case, just with CAD-derived reference data instead of video
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product description centers on authoring speed and cross-platform reach; not one mention of DDIL, offline sync, or disconnected content packaging in ~2,082 words of their own language
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our SaaS and on-prem platforms feature an AI-driven, no-code, platform agnostic XR authoring suite that integrates seamlessly with IoT and Digital Twins, supports remote assistance, and delivers valuable user analytics.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Their advocacy chain is operator-level fans, not program-office champions — 20+ years in and DoD wins are still SBIRs and pilots
blind_spots.operator_reality: A company commander loving EOD AR is not adoption; without a PM/PEO champion and a transition vehicle (P-8/V-22 program office line item), the 2022 Phase IIs die at period-of-performance end and the fleet never sees the tool
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Every DoD quote they showcase is from an individual engineer, HPT manager, or company commander — none from an acquisition authority; the org has no visible BD/capture or transition function at 29 people
blind_spots.evidence_quote: I'm a huge fan of EOD AR and the efforts your team is making.

opener_hook: Both of Avatar's 2022 Phase IIs — the Air Force NDE tool and the Navy V-22 SIA QA — are past their period of performance with no follow-on production vehicle visible on the public record.
what_they_do: 29-person XR/AR company whose no-code authoring platform builds maintenance and training applications for Navy, USMC, USCG, and industrial customers.
